speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is causing this, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if you have noticed any vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the baby been passing stool, and do you notice any specific smell or consistency to the stool? Also, please tell me if you have noticed any "currant jelly" colored stools or if the vomiting has been green?

REQUEST TEST: Stool analysis for reducing substances and occult blood.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the ultrasound and stool analysis are normal, let's explore the possibility of an anatomical obstruction. Have you noticed a palpable, worm-like mass moving in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal MRI with contrast.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound (repeat).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyloric Atresia.

Given the normal ultrasound ruling out hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, obstruction, and intussusception, the combination of early-onset feeding difficulties, severe abdominal distension, and bilious vomiting in an 8-month-old is most consistent with a congenital absence or atresia of the pylorus. Please confirm if any contrast study shows a cutoff at the gastric antrum.
